config.title: Vibe Coding as a Reconfiguration of Intent Mediation in Software Development: Definition, Implications, and Research Agenda
config.author: Christian Meske, Tobias Hermanns, Esther von der Weiden, Kai-Uwe Loser, Thorsten Berger

must_include_phrases: Software development is undergoing a fundamental transformation as vibe coding becomes widespread, with large portions of contemporary codebases now being generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI)
vibe coding as a software development paradigm where humans and Generative AI (GenAI) engage in collaborative flow to co-create software artifacts through natural language dialogue
By the 1980s, growing software complexity strained procedural code [21], [23]. Object-oriented programming (OOP) emerged to address this by redefining intent mediation around objects

Rather than merely executing predefined instructions, it participates in the interpretation of the developer's expressed intent, actively participates in knowledge construction, interpretation of requirements, and collaborative sensemaking
must_exclude_phrases: C. Meske et al.: Vibe Coding as a Reconfiguration of Intent Mediation in Software Development
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Ruhr University Bochum
notes: Published in IEEE Access (DOI: 10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3645466), received 31 October 2025, accepted 6 December 2025 (18 pages total). Research paper from Ruhr University Bochum (Germany) examining the emergence of vibe coding—a new software development paradigm enabled by Generative AI. Text density 1.0 (full embedded text layer). Two-column IEEE-style academic format with technical content on AI-mediated software development. Estimated 329 paragraphs based on page sampling; ±20% tolerance applied. Contains 6 figures/tables illustrating paradigm shifts, intent mediation concepts, and comparative analysis. Primary topics: democratization of software development, accelerated development cycles, responsibility gaps, ecosystem bias, and future research agenda. Authors from Mechanical Engineering and Computer Science faculties. Note: Two-column format particularly challenging around technical diagrams and transition between definitions/implications sections. Reading order critical for table content (e.g., Intent Mediation timelines, Traditional vs. Vibe Coding comparisons).
